issues.legal_issue: A tenant is not in default for claimed rent arrears when the landlord holds an excess advance that is immediately payable to the tenant and exceeds the arrears.
material_facts: The lease required a large advance, part of which was to be adjusted against rent and the balance repaid at the end of the lease.
The landlord continued to hold the balance of the advance when seeking eviction for alleged unpaid rent.
The amount held by the landlord exceeded the rent arrears claimed.
issues.conclusion: The excess advance was payable to the tenant immediately because the stipulation postponing its repayment was null and void. The tenant could not be treated as a defaulter for the claimed smaller amount, so eviction on that ground could not be sustained.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7(2)(a) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, a landlord may not receive or stipulate for an advance exceeding one month's rent; section 7(2)(b) requires an excess sum to be refunded or, at the tenant's option, adjusted; and section 7(3) makes a contrary stipulation null and void. The excess held by the landlord therefore became payable to the tenant immediately. The Court applied the reasoning in Mohd. Salimuddin v. Misri Lal & Anr., [1986] 1 SCR 622, and M/s. Sarwan Kumar Onkar Nath v. Subhas Kumar Agarwalla, [1987] 4 SCC 546, that a tenant is not in default where a prohibited advance held by the landlord is available to meet the claimed rent arrears.

rule.if: eviction_sought_for_rent_default and advance_exceeded_permitted_limit and landlord_held_excess_for_tenant and held_amount_exceeded_claimed_arrears

predicates.eviction_sought_for_rent_default: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.advance_exceeded_permitted_limit: The tenant paid an advance exceeding the amount the applicable law permits the landlord to receive as an advance.
predicates.landlord_held_excess_for_tenant: The landlord continued to hold the excess advance for the tenant when eviction was sought.
predicates.held_amount_exceeded_claimed_arrears: The amount the landlord held for the tenant exceeded the rent arrears claimed.

issues.definition: When eviction is sought for rent default and the landlord holds for the tenant a prohibited excess advance greater than the claimed arrears, the tenant is not in default for those arrears.

issues.legal_issue: Eviction cannot be ordered against a tenant under an unexpired fixed-term contractual lease when the lease contains no forfeiture clause terminating the tenancy.
material_facts: The lease granted a fixed term of thirty years that had not expired when eviction was sought.
The lease contained no forfeiture clause.
The lease had not been terminated, and the tenant remained in contractual possession.
issues.conclusion: The contractual tenancy was subsisting under the Transfer of Property Act, and eviction could not be ordered from that tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Transfer of Property Act, a fixed-term contractual tenancy continues while its term remains unexpired unless it is terminated in a legally effective manner. In the absence of a forfeiture clause leading to termination by forfeiture under section 111(g), eviction could not be ordered from the subsisting tenancy.

rule.if: eviction_sought_during_fixed_term_lease and lease_term_unexpired and no_forfeiture_clause and lease_not_terminated

predicates.eviction_sought_during_fixed_term_lease: A landlord sought eviction while the tenant occupied the premises under a fixed-term lease.
predicates.lease_term_unexpired: The lease term had not ended when eviction was sought.
predicates.no_forfeiture_clause: The lease contained no clause providing for termination by forfeiture.
predicates.lease_not_terminated: The lease had not otherwise been terminated before eviction was sought.

issues.definition: If eviction is sought during an unexpired fixed-term lease that contains no forfeiture clause and has not otherwise been terminated, eviction is unavailable against the subsisting tenancy.
